question: GQ-006
subject: two of the nine untraced runtime failures, both involving the vault

agentbase.error: Error: EPERM: process.cwd failed with error operation not permitted, uv_cwd
agentbase.diagnosis: Node cannot read its own working directory. The path EXISTS and my shell cd's into it fine — the difference is that launchd agents do not inherit Full Disk Access, which macOS requires for /Volumes. A permissions boundary, not a missing file.
agentbase.evidence: (cd /Volumes/.../agentbase && pwd) succeeds from an interactive shell; the same directory is EPERM to the launchd process.
agentbase.fixable_by: Granting Full Disk Access to the launchd context, or moving the working directory off the external volume. Both are Shaan decisions.

property_classq.diagnosis: The path contains "SISO-STORAGE-VAULT 1" — a macOS remount artifact. When a volume is mounted while an old mount point is still held, macOS appends a number. The job's path was frozen against that transient name.
property_classq.fixable_by: Editing one path in the plist to drop " 1". The script is present and intact.
property_classq.why_this_matters: Unlike the 26 deleted-path jobs, nothing is lost here. This is a stale reference to a mount that healed.

pattern: Both jobs that touch /Volumes fail, for two DIFFERENT reasons: one a permissions boundary, one a remount artifact. Nothing on the external volume is reliably reachable from launchd, which is worth knowing given the vault holds every Library backup.
